Question 2

q2 <- flights |> 
  filter(month == 1) |> 
    group_by(carrier) |> 
      summarise(mean_distance = mean(distance, na.rm = TRUE), 
                standard_deviation_distance = sd(distance, na.rm = TRUE)
                ) |> 
        arrange(mean_distance)

For carrier OO the standard deviation is NA because there is only one data entry, thus there is no deviation that can be determined therefore making it non applicable/NA. This is not the case however, for carriers such as YV, HA, etc. this is because all of their trips went the exact same distance and thus there was no deviation across the mean for the carriers, thus leaving it as the same value as the mean.

# 6.2

multi_flight_group <- flights |> 
  group_by(origin, dest) |> 
    filter(n_distinct(carrier)>1)


avg_delay_df <- multi_flight_group |> 
  group_by(origin, dest, carrier) |> 
    summarise(
      avg_arrival_delay = mean(arr_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = 'drop') |> 
        filter(!is.na(avg_arrival_delay)) |> 
          arrange(origin, dest, avg_arrival_delay)

avg_delay_df <- avg_delay_df |> inner_join(airlines, by = 'carrier')

      worst_airlines = carrier[which.max(avg_arrival_delay)],

# 6.4


route_performance <- avg_delay_df |> 
  group_by(origin, dest) |> 
    summarise(
      best_airline = carrier[which.min(avg_arrival_delay)],  # Airline with least delay
      worst_airline = carrier[which.max(avg_arrival_delay)], # Airline with most delay
      best_delay = min(avg_arrival_delay, na.rm = TRUE),  # Best delay
      worst_delay = max(avg_arrival_delay, na.rm = TRUE), # Worst delay
      delay_diff = worst_delay - best_delay,  # Difference in performance
      .groups = 'drop'
    )

worst_route <- route_performance |> 
  arrange(desc(delay_diff)) |>
    slice(1)  

kable(worst_route)
origin dest best_airline worst_airline best_delay worst_delay delay_diff
JFK ATL 9E EV 1.403846 128 126.5962 
# The worst route is thus JFK to ATL performed by carrier 9E
